**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), June 2019, ADVANCED LEVEL. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure considered as an attempt to cheat will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorized composition will earn you no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown: **SECTION A: SUMMARY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION (30 marks)**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**QUESTION 1: SUMMARY (15 marks)**

Read the following passage carefully, and summarise it in two paragraphs of not more than 150 words.

Few fish grab our attention the way the clown fish does. Perhaps it wins our hearts with its fancy colouring, which may remind us of a circus clown, or maybe we are struck by its surprising choice of home - among the stinging tentacles of a sea anemone. Not surprising, another name for the clown fish is anemone fish. Like many Hollywood actors, clown fish are not averse to photographs. Divers and snorkelers can usually expect clown fish to "pose" for pictures, since they rarely stray far from home and are not particularly shy.

But what makes the clown fish extraordinary is their seemingly risky lifestyle. Living among poisonous tentacles would seem to be comparable to setting up a home in a nest of serpents. Still, clown fish and their anemone of choice are inseparable. Like most good partnerships, clown fish and anemones give and take. The relationship is not merely convenient for the clown fish; it is vital in that they are poor swimmers and would be at the mercy of hungry predators without the anemone's protection. By using the anemone as a home base and as a safe shelter when threatened, the clown fish may reach ten years of age. The anemone provides a safe nesting site as well as a home. The clown fish deposit their eggs at the base of the host anemone, where both parents keep watch over them. Later, the clown fish family can be seen swimming around that same anemone.

The clown fish serve as marine bodyguards, driving away butterfly fish that like to feed on anemone tentacles. At least one species of anemone cannot leave without resident clown fish. When researchers removed the clown fish, within just twenty-four hours, the anemones had disappeared completely. Apparently, butterfly fish had consumed them. It seems that clown fish even provide their host with energy. The ammonium that clown fish excrete helps spur growth in the host anemone. And as the clown fish swim among the tentacles, they help circulate oxygen-rich water to the anemone.

Some studies suggest that when selecting a new host, the clown fish goes through a process of adaptation. It has been observed that when the fish approaches an anemone for the first time, it touches the anemone intermittently for few hours. This on-and-off contact allows the clown fish to modify its protective coating to conform to the new anemone's particular poison. Possibly the clown fish gets stung a little during this process. But after that, the two get along fine. The collaboration of such different creatures offers a fascinating lesson in teamwork. In so many human endeavours, people from diverse cultures and backgrounds achieve remarkable results by pooling their resources. Like the clown fish, we may take a little time to adapt to working with others, but the results are well worth it.

*Adapted from Awake! No. 6 of 2016*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model summary (138 words, two paragraphs)**

Clown fish are admired for their bright colours and for living unharmed among the poisonous tentacles of sea anemones, which they rarely leave and near which they pose willingly for divers. The partnership is vital to them. Being poor swimmers, they find protection from predators, which allows them to live for up to ten years, and a secure place where both parents guard the eggs.

In return, the fish drive away butterfly fish that eat the anemone; one species even vanished within a day without them. Their waste ammonium stimulates growth and their swimming brings the anemone oxygenated water. When choosing a new host, a fish repeatedly touches it so that its protective coating adapts to the poison. Such cooperation teaches that people from varied backgrounds can achieve much by adapting to one another and pooling their resources.

**Content points expected**

1. Clown fish are striking (colour) and live among the stinging tentacles of a sea anemone without harm.
2. They stay close to home and are not shy, so divers can photograph them.
3. The partnership is vital: the fish are poor swimmers and the anemone protects them from predators, so they can live up to ten years.
4. The anemone is also a nesting site: the eggs are laid at its base and both parents guard them.
5. The fish protect the anemone by driving away butterfly fish; without them one species disappeared within twenty-four hours.
6. The fish feed the anemone (ammonium helps growth) and circulate oxygen-rich water.
7. A new host is approached gradually: repeated contact lets the fish adapt its coating to the anemone's poison.
8. The lesson: people of different backgrounds can achieve great results by cooperating and adapting.

**Marking grid (indicative; the split of the 15 marks is not printed on the paper)**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Content | The main points above, accurate and in a logical order, with the examples and details left out |
| Own words | Rephrasing of the passage (for example "live unharmed among" for "living among poisonous tentacles"), not copied strings |
| Expression and accuracy | Two clear paragraphs, correct grammar, connectors, and respect of the 150-word limit |

**Common mistakes**

1. Copying whole sentences from the passage (this earns no marks) or exceeding 150 words.
2. Writing one paragraph instead of two, or adding personal comments and the title "Summary" as if it were the answer's content.

incertitudes: Consigne de la page de garde (règle de choix) : « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet ». Section A obligatoire (aucune règle), Section B : 1 sujet sur 6 (a à f), Section C : 1 question sur 4. Les regles_choix sont identiques dans les 12 fichiers.

Fautes imprimées dans le sujet, laissées telles quelles : titre « SECTION A SUMMERY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION » (summary), « for few hours » (Q1), « A this stage », « into the will » (mill), « The stripped cane are then », « out of them » (Q2, forme reconstruite) ; Section C question 2 : « Use any Three prescribed text ».
Le tiret cadratin du passage de résumé (« choice of home - among the stinging tentacles ») est écrit « - » conformément à la règle du projet. Le passage ne porte pas de numéros de ligne imprimés.

Section A : le sujet imprime 30 marks pour la section (15 par question). La répartition des 15 points du résumé n'est pas imprimée : la grille du corrigé est indicative. La reconstruction est comptée à 1 point par blanc (15 blancs), ce qui est une hypothèse ; plusieurs réponses sont acceptables pour certains blancs (voir le corrigé).

Section B : 20 marks (Content and Organisation 6, Expression 8, Accuracy 6), 500 à 550 mots demandés. Points imprimés non corrigés. Compositions modèles : comptes de mots faits par script (de 517 à 534 mots).
